quotes.text: Amos was evidently a common man of the land (Amos 7:14-15), called by the Lord about seventy years before northern Israel's exile. He warned the leaders and the people of imminent destruction and sought to save them, saying, "Seek good, and not evil, that ye may live" (Amos 5:14). The word saw in verse 1 is used to translate the Hebrew chazah, which denotes divine vision, not ordinary sight. The metaphor of a lion roaring in warning, "The Lord will roar from Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem" (v. 2), was also used by other prophets (Amos 1:2a; Joel 3:16). The temple in Jerusalem was a place for the Lord's communication with them. There is symbolism also in warnings going out from the mountain of the Lord's house in Judah, addressed to the high, beautiful, and productive Mount Carmel in northern Israel. The withering of Carmel's top represents the deterioration of the highest political and religious leaders of northern Israel who were the cause of many of her ills. The earthquake mentioned by Amos and again by Zechariah (Amos 1:1c) two and one-half centuries later must have been a notable event in the days of King Uzziah.
quotes.speaker: Ellis T. Rasmussen
quotes.source: A Latter-day Saint Commentary on the Old Testament
quotes.attr: Ellis T. Rasmussen, A Latter-day Saint Commentary on the Old Testament, p.644
